payload.mdAr:
Insurance rarely pays everything. What the member owes is decided by a small set of mechanisms that behave differently from one another, and most confusion at a front desk comes from treating them as one thing called "the patient's share".

The order matters and is worth memorising: deductible first, then coinsurance, and both are bounded by the out-of-pocket maximum. A copay may sit outside that sequence altogether depending on the plan.

payload.defAr: A fixed amount for a defined service. Known in advance and unchanged by the cost of the encounter, which is why it is the easiest to explain and to collect.
payload.defEn: A fixed amount for a defined service. Known in advance and unchanged by the cost of the encounter, which is why it is the easiest to explain and to collect.

payload.defAr: An amount the member pays before the policy shares cost at all, accumulating across the policy year.
payload.defEn: An amount the member pays before the policy shares cost at all, accumulating across the policy year.
payload.exampleAr: A member early in the year may be told a service is covered and still owe the full amount: covered and payable are not the same thing.
payload.exampleEn: A member early in the year may be told a service is covered and still owe the full amount: covered and payable are not the same thing.

payload.defAr: A percentage of the allowed amount, applied after the deductible is met. Because it is a percentage, the figure cannot be known until the payer has priced the service.
payload.defEn: A percentage of the allowed amount, applied after the deductible is met. Because it is a percentage, the figure cannot be known until the payer has priced the service.

payload.defAr: A ceiling on the member's own spending. Once reached, the policy pays the remainder for the rest of the year. Premiums do not count toward it.
payload.defEn: A ceiling on the member's own spending. Once reached, the policy pays the remainder for the rest of the year. Premiums do not count toward it.

payload.mdAr:
Training figures only. An encounter is allowed at 4,800. The member has 1,000 of deductible remaining and 20% coinsurance.

They pay the 1,000, then 20% of the remaining 3,800, which is 760. Their liability is 1,760 and the payer pays 3,040 — unless that 1,760 would carry them past their out-of-pocket maximum, in which case the ceiling applies and the payer pays more.

payload.mdAr: The most expensive misreading is treating "limited" as "covered". The service is genuinely in the schedule, the member is genuinely eligible, and the claim is still refused because the limit was already reached. Nothing on the card or in an eligibility response shows this — it requires checking accumulated use.

payload.mdAr: "Covered" is the word members hear as "free". Never use it alone. "Covered, and your share will be X" is a different sentence, and it prevents most of the arguments that follow a bill.
